nodes.name: base.py
nodes.summary: Defines queue-worker registration, queue assignment, restart signaling, exception policy, metrics, and reusable single-event and looping worker bases.
nodes.languageNotes: Decorator-based registration and class-level queue metadata let the process supervisor discover worker implementations consistently.

nodes.name: assign_queue
nodes.summary: Attaches queue names and retry policy metadata to a worker class and registers it for discovery.

nodes.name: register_worker
nodes.summary: Registers a worker class under its configured queue name while rejecting duplicate declarations.

nodes.name: check_and_send_restart_signal
nodes.summary: Raises the worker restart signal after configuration changes or configured memory limits require recycling.

nodes.name: WorkerTimeoutError
nodes.summary: Represents the WorkerTimeout failure raised by queue worker infrastructure.

nodes.name: InterruptConsumeError
nodes.summary: Represents the InterruptConsume failure raised by queue worker infrastructure.

nodes.name: WorkerDeclarationError
nodes.summary: Represents the WorkerDeclaration failure raised by queue worker infrastructure.

nodes.name: QueueProcessingWorker
nodes.summary: Defines event validation, metrics, exception handling, queue consumption, and lifecycle behavior for one-event-at-a-time workers.

nodes.name: LoopQueueProcessingWorker
nodes.summary: Extends the worker base with periodic looping work interleaved with nonblocking queue consumption.

nodes.summary: Registers the deferred-email queue worker using the shared email-delivery implementation.

nodes.name: DeferredEmailSenderWorker
nodes.summary: Implements the DeferredEmailSenderWorker queue worker for deferred email delivery.

nodes.summary: Guides contributors through finding, evaluating, crediting, and presenting work that continues an existing unfinished issue or pull request.

nodes.name: design-discussions.md
nodes.summary: Sets expectations for inclusive, productive product-design discussions, with role-specific guidance for participants, contributors, moderators, and decision makers.

nodes.name: how-we-communicate.md
nodes.summary: Defines community communication norms for constructive suggestions, respectful disagreements, and meaningful expressions of appreciation.

layers.name: API Layer
layers.description: Django URL routing, views, serializers, OpenAPI contracts, and incoming webhook adapters that expose Zulip functionality.

layers.name: UI Layer
layers.description: Browser TypeScript and JavaScript, Django templates and forms, static styling and assets, localization catalogs, and the Starlight help frontend.

layers.name: Middleware Layer
layers.description: Django request middleware, authentication decorators, REST boundary helpers, and remote billing authentication controls.

layers.name: Service Layer
layers.description: Zulip domain actions, workers, signals, tasks, application packages, and orchestration that implement collaboration and billing behavior.

layers.name: Data Layer
layers.description: Django ORM models and migrations, analytics persistence, database schemas, SQL assets, and other stored-data definitions.

layers.name: Utility Layer
layers.description: Shared libraries, helpers, contracts, developer automation, maintenance scripts, and third-party compatibility patches used across the repository.

layers.name: Configuration Layer
layers.description: Django settings and entry points, app and management configuration, package manifests, and JSON, YAML, TOML, or toolchain settings.

layers.name: Test Layer
layers.description: Backend and frontend tests, integration fixtures, mocks, snapshots, and captured webhook or payment payloads that verify Zulip behavior.

layers.name: Infrastructure & CI/CD
layers.description: Puppet provisioning, Docker images and build stages, CI workflows, deployment resources, and runtime environment support.

layers.name: Documentation Layer
layers.description: Developer, administrator, integration, API, and end-user help content maintained across Markdown, MDX, RST, and related documentation assets.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with Zulip's README to understand its topic-based conversation model, the clients it supports, and the paths for trying, deploying, or developing the product. This overview supplies the product vocabulary and roadmap for the runtime, data, messaging, and operations layers that follow.

tour.title: Web Application Bootstrap
tour.description: With the product's purpose established, follow the main browser bundle as it loads setup code, feature modules, plugins, and styles. The UI initializer then activates the web application's subsystems, while the validated bootstrap state gives them a shared, typed view of server-provided data.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript types disappear at runtime, so Zod schemas at the JSON boundary validate real browser bootstrap data before the rest of the application relies on static types.

tour.title: Django Runtime Entrypoints
tour.description: The browser application from Step 2 is served by a Django backend whose administrative, production, and routing entrypoints are separated here. manage.py starts management commands, wsgi.py exposes the production application, and urls.py connects authentication, API, organization, integration, webhook, and static routes to their handlers.
tour.languageLesson: Django separates command-line startup from WSGI request startup; its URL configuration then composes route patterns into the view layer, keeping process bootstrapping distinct from HTTP dispatch.

tour.title: Core Domain Model
tour.description: Those routes operate on the central Django domain model, whose public model barrel exposes the entities used across the backend. Realm, user, stream, and subscription helpers encode the organization policies, identities, settings, and channel relationships that make Zulip's conversation model work.
tour.languageLesson: Django QuerySets are lazy: constructing or refining one does not query PostgreSQL until it is evaluated. This makes composable model helpers powerful, but hidden evaluation inside loops can create expensive N+1 query patterns.

tour.title: Typed API Boundary
tour.description: Building on the model vocabulary from Step 4, the HTTP boundary authenticates and authorizes callers, converts annotated request values, validates them, and returns consistent JSON responses. These shared decorators and typed endpoint utilities keep repetitive boundary concerns out of individual feature handlers while also supporting API documentation.
tour.languageLesson: Python decorators wrap endpoint functions to apply cross-cutting behavior such as authentication and request parsing, while annotations let the wrapper derive coercion and validation rules without duplicating them in every view.

tour.title: Message Delivery Pipeline
tour.description: A message-send request crosses the boundary from Step 5 through a thin view into the server-side delivery action. The pipeline validates recipients, constructs typed payloads, creates compact per-user visibility records, and accounts for mentions, bots, unread state, serialization, and push eligibility.
tour.languageLesson: In Django, keeping views focused on HTTP parsing and delegating state changes to action functions creates a reusable service boundary for API requests, tests, management commands, and background work.

tour.title: Real-Time Event Flow
tour.description: After Step 6 persists a message, the real-time subsystem turns backend changes into the event stream consumed by connected clients. Django workers publish through the bridge, Tornado and RabbitMQ maintain asynchronous delivery, client queues handle fanout and lifecycle, and typed event definitions preserve the server-to-browser protocol.
tour.languageLesson: Python TypedDict definitions describe dictionary-shaped event contracts to static type checkers without changing their JSON-compatible runtime representation, which is useful at a large protocol boundary.

tour.title: Client Message State
tour.description: The browser receives the stream from Step 7 through a central dispatcher that routes each event to the appropriate state update. Message-event handlers reconcile inserts, edits, moves, and deletions with the canonical message cache, while the view layer fetches, renders, and navigates the resulting feed.

tour.title: Optimistic Message Composition
tour.description: Step 8 explains incoming state; this cluster covers the outgoing user experience from composing and previewing through sending and scheduling. Echo inserts temporary local messages immediately, then reconciles server IDs or exposes retry failures, while notification logic determines post-send visibility and navigation behavior.

tour.title: Asynchronous Worker Queues
tour.description: Not every consequence of the message flow belongs on a request or real-time process, so Zulip publishes deferred work to RabbitMQ-backed queues. Reusable worker bases provide queue assignment, restart, metrics, and exception policy; the processor registry selects implementations, and the outgoing-webhook worker demonstrates how external integrations consume queued events.

tour.title: Database and Search
tour.description: The models and delivery pipeline ultimately rely on a PostgreSQL database created with a deliberate UTF-8 locale and application role. A separate setup script enables PGroonga, adding the multilingual full-text search capability needed by a global conversation product.
tour.languageLesson: PostgreSQL extensions add database-native capabilities beyond standard SQL, but they become an explicit deployment dependency. Encoding and locale choices made when a database is created also affect text comparison and search behavior later.

tour.title: Production Architecture
tour.description: With the application and persistence layers understood, the architecture guide places Django, Tornado, nginx, Supervisor, caches, queues, PostgreSQL, and monitoring into one production system. The deployment guide covers supported installation shapes and network concerns, while the production workflow verifies fresh installs, upgrades, and build artifacts across supported operating systems.

tour.title: Development and CI
tour.description: The local development environment mirrors enough of Step 12's system to support work across several virtualization providers, with forwarded ports, proxies, synchronized Git data, and provisioning. CI supplies an unprivileged container image and a broad matrix covering backend, frontend, documentation, schemas, typing, linting, coverage, and database checks.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions matrices expand one YAML job definition into parallel test variants, while Docker layer ordering determines cache reuse; stable system dependencies should precede frequently changing project code.

tour.title: Contributor Workflow
tour.description: The final stop turns the architecture into a practical contribution path, covering setup, issue selection, collaboration, pull requests, and project policy. The code-style guide defines safety and testing expectations, and the staged review process explains the labels and follow-up practices that move changes from proposal to merge.
